subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A fast shutter speed is most useful for...
questions.explain: A fast shutter speed freezes rapid action, capturing it as a crisp, sharp image.

questions.q: What does ISO measure on a camera?
questions.explain: ISO sets the sensor's sensitivity to light; a high ISO brightens images but can add noise.

questions.q: In film photography, in which room is light-sensitive paper developed?
questions.explain: Film and prints are processed in a darkroom, where safelight prevents the paper being fogged.

questions.q: A high ISO setting tends to introduce what into an image?
questions.explain: Raising the ISO brightens the image but increases visible noise or grain.

questions.q: What does shutter speed mainly control?
options: The length of time light hits the sensor
questions.explain: Shutter speed sets how long the sensor is exposed to light, affecting motion blur and brightness.

questions.q: Which genre focuses on capturing real events and everyday life truthfully?
questions.explain: Documentary photography records real events, people and life as honestly as possible.

questions.q: Why might a photographer use editing 'layers'?
options: To reduce the file to one flat image instantly
To stack and adjust separate elements independently
questions.explain: Layers let an editor stack and adjust separate elements without permanently altering the others.

questions.q: A 'still life' photograph typically shows...
questions.explain: Still life depicts a deliberate arrangement of inanimate objects, such as fruit or bottles.

questions.q: In photography, 'cropping' an image means...
options: Cutting away parts of the frame to improve composition
questions.explain: Cropping removes unwanted edges to tighten or rebalance the composition.

questions.q: Shooting from a low viewpoint looking up tends to make a subject appear...
questions.explain: A low viewpoint looking up can make a subject seem larger, dominant or more imposing.

questions.q: A 'photogram' is made by...
options: Placing objects on light-sensitive paper and exposing it to light
questions.explain: A photogram is a cameraless image made by laying objects on photographic paper and exposing it to light.

questions.q: What is 'depth of field'?
options: The range of the scene that appears in sharp focus
The distance from the camera to the subject
questions.explain: Depth of field is how much of the scene, from front to back, appears acceptably sharp.

questions.q: What is a 'contact sheet' used for in photography?
options: Viewing many small thumbnail images to select the best shots
questions.explain: A contact sheet shows small versions of all the frames so the photographer can choose which to develop.

questions.q: 'Saturation' in an image describes...
options: The intensity or purity of the colours
questions.explain: Saturation measures how vivid or intense the colours are; low saturation looks washed out.

questions.q: A slow shutter speed used on moving water typically creates...
questions.explain: A slow shutter speed records movement over time, smoothing flowing water into a soft blur.

questions.q: Which photographer is famous for dramatic black-and-white landscapes of the American West, such as Yosemite?
questions.explain: Ansel Adams is renowned for his sharp, high-contrast black-and-white landscape photographs.

questions.q: A 'silhouette' is created when the subject is...
options: Dark against a bright background, showing only its outline
questions.explain: A silhouette appears when a backlit subject is rendered dark, revealing only its shape.

questions.q: Photographing a subject from directly above is known as a...
questions.explain: A bird's-eye or flat-lay viewpoint looks straight down on the subject from above.

questions.q: 'The exposure triangle' refers to the relationship between...
questions.explain: Aperture, shutter speed and ISO together control exposure and form the exposure triangle.

questions.q: A 'photomontage' is created by...
options: Combining parts of several photographs into one image
questions.explain: A photomontage assembles fragments of several photographs into a single composite image.

questions.q: Increasing the 'contrast' of a photo does what?
options: Makes darks darker and lights lighter
questions.explain: Increasing contrast widens the difference between the lightest and darkest tones.

questions.q: In a portrait, lighting placed to one side to create strong shadows and modelling is called...
questions.explain: Side lighting rakes across the face, producing shadows that reveal form and texture.
